_meta.what: Tree and shrub species of the plain and the town gardens (Phase 7 / Phase 6 planting), and the proportions the tree generator (src/world/trees/model.ts) builds them to.
_meta.tiers: presence: the species' presence in the Marvdasht plain or the gardens in 467 BCE, with its own tier and source (pollen, PF commodities, riparian analogy). form: height, crown width / height, crown base / height (lowest foliage), trunk diameter at breast height / height, number of stems, crown shape and branching habit. Every form value is C: general dendrology recalled by the builder (source key BOTANY-GEN), not read in a flora this session; it describes mature, open-grown trees of the species as they grow today.
_meta.fields: height_m [min, max] (m); crown_width_ratio [min, max] = crown diameter / height; crown_base_ratio [min, max] = height of the lowest foliage / height; dbh_ratio = trunk diameter at 1.3 m / height (each stem of a multi-stem tree: the ratio x 0.6); stems [min, max] from the ground; habit: excurrent (a central leader to the top) or decurrent (the trunk divides into limbs at the crown base); envelope: widest (height fraction of the crown's widest ring), top / bottom (superellipse exponents of the upper and lower crown); limb_angle_deg (primary limbs from the vertical); droop (0 upswept .. 1 hanging outer shoots); leaf: tile (leaf-cluster texture), size_cm (leaf blade length), layers (leaf-card layers over the crown surface: density of the canopy); bark: albedo (sRGB-encoded, C); blossom tile (null: no showy blossom).
_meta.src_note: BOTANY-GEN is recollection (tier C). Presence sources: IR-RIPARIAN (modern riparian community of the Zayandeh-Rud, analogy B), SAEIDI2021 (Maharlou pollen: Platanus, Olea, Punica, cypress with Achaemenid arboriculture; Quercus and Pistacia-Amygdalus on the slopes, B), IR-FOODAG (PF fruits: figs, apples, pears, mulberries, pistachios; wine, B).

species.name: oriental plane (Platanus orientalis)

presence.note: riparian dominant of Iranian plateau rivers today (analogy); Platanus pollen with Achaemenid arboriculture

species.note: a broad spreading dome on a short, thick bole; limbs spread wide from 3-6 m; bark flakes in grey, cream and olive patches; deeply 5-lobed leaves 10-20 cm

species.name: white willow (Salix alba)

presence.note: riparian tree of Iranian plateau rivers today (analogy)

species.note: rounded, rather open crown on a short, often leaning or forked trunk; limbs upswept, the outer shoots hang; narrow leaves silvery beneath, so the crown reads grey-green

species.name: poplar (Populus alba / P. nigra)

presence.note: Populus in the riparian woodland of Iranian plateau rivers today (analogy); which species and whether the narrow planted form existed in 467 is open (Q-170)

species.note: a straight leader to the top with short, steeply ascending branches: a narrow oval crown (C: the planted narrow form, Q-170); triangular leaves on flat stalks

species.name: tamarisk (Tamarix ramosissima)

presence.note: Tamarix ramosissima shrubs along Iranian plateau rivers today (analogy)

species.note: a multi-stemmed shrub of slender reddish stems fanning from the ground; feathery, drooping sprays of tiny scale leaves, blue-grey green

species.name: mulberry (Morus nigra / M. alba)

presence.note: mulberries among the PF fruit commodities

species.note: a dense rounded dome about as wide as tall on a short, rough-barked trunk; heart-shaped leaves

species.name: fig (Ficus carica)

presence.note: figs among the PF fruit commodities

species.note: low and spreading, wider than tall, several smooth pale-grey stems; thick stubby twigs; large 3-5-lobed leaves in a coarse, rather open canopy; no showy flowers

species.name: apple (Malus domestica, old cultivated form)

presence.note: apples among the PF fruit commodities

species.note: a rounded, open crown on a short trunk; ovate leaves; white-pink blossom on the spurs in April

species.name: pear (Pyrus communis s.l.)

presence.note: pears among the PF fruit commodities

species.note: upright, narrower than apple, a leader with ascending branches (an oval to broad-pyramidal crown); dark, finely checked bark; white blossom in late March and April

species.name: pomegranate (Punica granatum)
species.note: a many-stemmed shrubby small tree, fine twiggy and dense; small narrow glossy leaves; scarlet flowers from May

species.name: Brant's oak (Quercus brantii)

presence.note: oak pollen of the Zagros woodland in the late Holocene

species.note: a short tree, often several stems from an old cut stool, with an open, irregular crown wider than tall (woodland rule: crowns 5-9 m, 4-8 m tall); oblong toothed leaves, grey-green and felted

species.name: wild almond (Amygdalus scoparia / A. lycioides)

presence.note: Pistacia-Amygdalus scrub pollen on the slopes

species.note: a broom-like shrub of many erect, green switch stems with few small leaves; pale pink blossom in February and March

species.name: wild pistachio (Pistacia atlantica)

presence.note: Pistacia pollen on the slopes; pistachios among the PF commodities

species.note: a stout short trunk under a dense, rounded crown; pinnate leaves; reddish in autumn

species.name: cypress (Cupressus sempervirens)
species.note: the narrow upright form planted in gardens (C: the wild form of Iran is broader, Q-171); dense dark scale-leaf foliage to the ground, evergreen

species.name: olive (Olea europaea)
species.note: a broad, irregular crown on a short, gnarled grey trunk; narrow leaves grey-green above, silvery below; evergreen

species.name: grape vine (Vitis vinifera), head-trained

presence.note: wine of several kinds in PF

species.note: a low vine on its own short trunk (head-trained, C), canes spreading and bending; lobed leaves
